header.title: Swan House Farm
header.subtitle: Early Fall
header.tagline: thank you so much for joining us on this humble journey through everything skagit and swan house has to offer

courses.label: Antipasti
courses.subtitle: passed welcome bites at sit-down
courses.plateware: Two bites passed together at sit-down. Per setting: 8" bread plate and fork only. Cutlery is staggered course-by-course, not all preset at once. Crudo held cold at the pass and passed fast; figs passed warm off the grill.

dishes.name: Salmon Crudo
dishes.components: corn crema, red cabbage kimchi, fresh padrón, gluten free grain cracker
dishes.story: Salmon served raw and cold on a crisp gluten free grain cracker. Underneath it, a smooth crema of sweet Skagit corn; over it, a little of the red cabbage kimchi we started at the farm with Kelly's own cabbage, and a ring of fresh padrón pepper. Sweet, cool, fermented and green in one bite, and naturally gluten free.

ingredients.note: Italian for raw; fish served cold and simply dressed, the Italian cousin of sashimi
a small green Spanish frying pepper, grown here at Swan House; mostly gentle, occasionally one runs hot, which is half the fun
cabbage fermented with chili and aromatics; ours is made at the farm from the farm's own red cabbage

dishes.name: Grilled Fig and Guanciale
dishes.components: Swan House fig, farm guanciale, saba, fennel pollen
dishes.story: A fig from the farm's own Desert King tree, grilled until it just slumps, draped with a thin slice of guanciale we cured here at the farm, and finished with saba and fennel pollen. The fig tree and the cure live a few hundred feet from your table.

ingredients.note: pork jowl cured with salt and pepper, the cut that makes carbonara carbonara; ours is cured at Swan House
grape must cooked slowly down to a dark, sweet-tart syrup; balsamic's ancient, gentler cousin
the fig variety that actually ripens in the Pacific Northwest, green skinned with deep pink flesh; these come off the farm's own tree
the dried flower pollen of wild fennel; a little dusts on like honeyed anise

courses.label: Insalata
courses.subtitle: course one
courses.plateware: Plated cold, farm-side build. Salad plate, fork and butter knife (thick-cut tomato).

dishes.name: Farm Tomato Caprese
dishes.components: peak farm tomatoes, Ferndale Farmstead mozzarella, garden basil, toasted focaccia crumb, tomato leaf oil
dishes.story: September is the month the farm's tomatoes hit their absolute peak, so this course stays out of their way. Thick-cut farm tomatoes, fresh mozzarella from Ferndale Farmstead up in Whatcom County, and basil we grew a few rows from your table and kept off the restaurant's menus so there would be enough for these dinners. Over the top, a crumb of toasted Breadfarm focaccia, a green oil made from the tomato plants' own leaves, and balsamic.

ingredients.note: a farmstead creamery in Ferndale, Whatcom County, making Italian-style cheeses entirely from their own herd's milk; about as local as mozzarella gets
olive oil infused with the leaves of the tomato plants themselves; it tastes the way a tomato vine smells
the Edison bakery a few miles from the farm; their focaccia is toasted into the golden crumb on this plate

courses.label: Primi
courses.subtitle: course two
courses.plateware: Warm bowl, fork and spoon. Finished in batches at the pass — par-cooked campanelle finished to order in the clam butter.

dishes.name: Squid Ink Campanelle, Steamers and Chanterelles
dishes.components: squid ink campanelle, steamer clams, golden chanterelles, grilled corn, clam butter
dishes.story: Campanelle means little bells: a ruffled, trumpet-shaped pasta, extruded by hand at San Fermo and turned black with squid ink. It cooks into a broth built from the steamer clams' own liquor, mounted with butter, and carries the clams, golden chanterelles, and kernels of grilled local corn. September is the best chanterelle month of the year in the Northwest woods, and this is the plate they were picked for.

ingredients.note: 'little bells' — a short ruffled pasta shape that holds broth in its folds; ours is extruded fresh at the restaurant
the ink of the squid, kneaded into the dough; it turns the pasta jet black and adds a gentle savory brine, not fishiness
small sweet Northwest clams cooked in the shell; their liquor becomes the sauce
the Northwest's signature wild mushroom, apricot-scented and meaty; September is its finest hour

courses.label: Secondi
courses.subtitle: course three
courses.plateware: Shared board for two: the steak sliced, romesco and cucumber-mint salad on the board. Steak knife and fork per setting. Kitchen-finished and batch-fired; nothing is carved in the room.

dishes.name: Swan House Beef, Steak for Two
dishes.components: green pepper romesco, cold cucumber and mint salad
dishes.story: The farm's own beef. Tim raises the cattle here at Swan House, and the steaks are cut right at the farm: one 16-ounce steak shared between each pair of guests, rib eye and New York across the tables, reverse-seared low and slow and finished over apple wood on the Big Green Egg. Alongside it, a romesco built green from the farm's September peppers, and a cold salad of Kelly's cucumbers and mint to keep the plate fresh.

ingredients.note: a rustic Catalan pepper sauce, traditionally brick red; ours is built green from the sweet and frying peppers coming out of the garden right now
the steak cooks gently in a low oven first, then finishes hard over apple wood; edge-to-edge rosy instead of a thin band of doneness
raised on this property by Tim; the herd lives on the pastures you walked past on the way in

courses.label: Dolce
courses.subtitle: course four
courses.plateware: Small bowl and small spoon. Gelato scooped at the pass, warm apple butter and crumble on top; goes out fast.

dishes.name: Toasted Fig Leaf Gelato
dishes.components: warm King apple butter, olive oil cake crumble
dishes.story: The same fig tree that gave you the welcome bite gives up its leaves for dessert. Toasted until fragrant and steeped into the gelato base, fig leaf tastes of coconut and vanilla, a flavor you can only really get from a tree you have access to. The gelato lands over a spoonful of warm apple butter made from the farm's first King apples of the fall, with a crumble of dehydrated olive oil cake for crunch. Cold, warm and crisp in the same bite.

ingredients.note: toasted and steeped like a tea into the cream; it gives coconut and vanilla notes, no figs required — though ours come from the same tree as the fig on your first bite
an old Northwest heirloom apple, one of the first to ripen at the farm each fall; cooked slowly down into the warm apple butter under the gelato

courses.label: Caffé
courses.subtitle: to close
courses.plateware: Cups and saucers, poured tableside as dessert lands.

dishes.name: Cafe Umbria
dishes.story: Locally roasted coffee from Seattle's Cafe Umbria, served to close the meal.

wines.name: Bellenda ‘San Fermo’ Valdobbiadene Prosecco Superiore DOCG
wines.pour_notes: The arrival pour, and the one with the best story on the list: the cuvée is called San Fermo, after the little country church that sits beside the vineyard the grapes come from. Same name as the restaurant, entirely by coincidence. A fine, dense, continuous bead; delicate and fragrant, with a vein of minerality and a crisp walnut-husk tang on the finish. Brut, so it comes in dry rather than sweet. Pour it properly cold, 6-8°C, in a big glass rather than a flute.
wines.producer: Bellenda works the steep Conegliano Valdobbiadene hills of the Veneto, the historic heart of Prosecco and the part of the zone that earns the Superiore designation. The San Fermo fruit comes off Carpesica, on limestone-clay soils full of morainic deposits left by the ancient Piave glacier, facing south-southwest at about 180 meters and planted at 4,000 vines per hectare. The name is the country church next to the vineyard.
wines.winemaking: Glera, second fermentation in the Italian (Charmat) method in 100hl stainless pressure tanks over roughly two months, with time on the lees. Millesimato means it is a single-vintage bottling rather than the usual multi-vintage blend. 7 g/L residual sugar puts it squarely in Brut.

wines.name: La Spinetta ‘Casanova della Spinetta’ Vermentino
wines.pour_notes: The white for September, replacing August's Friulian Sauvignon. Vermentino is the coastal white of Tuscany, Liguria and Sardinia: pale straw, smelling of citrus peel, white flowers and Mediterranean scrub, with a saline, faintly bitter-almond finish that reads as sea air. Dry, fresh and light on its feet. It is built for the first half of this table: the salmon crudo with corn and kimchi, the caprese, and especially the steamer clams and squid ink campanelle, where a salty coastal white does what the lemon would otherwise do. Frosted bottle, Dürer's rhinoceros on the label. Pour it cold, 10-12°C.
wines.producer: La Spinetta started in Piedmont and is best known there, but Casanova della Spinetta is their Tuscan estate at Terricciola, inland from Pisa. The estate runs roughly 57 acres at 250 meters on sandy ground rich in ancient oceanic sediment, facing southeast, with vines averaging about twenty years old. The grapes are certified organic (Valoritalia) and the estate carries a sustainable-farming certification. Produced by La Spinetta at Castagnole delle Lanze and bottled at Casanova della Spinetta in Terricciola.
wines.winemaking: Made with certified organic grapes (Valoritalia) and certified vegan. Fermented and rested in stainless steel with no oak, the same clean, fruit-first approach as the estate's rosato, so the citrus, the flowers and the salinity stay in front. Imported by Indigenous Selections.

wines.name: Fabrizio Pratesi ‘Locorosso’
wines.pour_notes: Pure Sangiovese from Carmignano, and — like everything else on this list — no oak on it. Deep ruby, with strawberry, cherry and black currant, a dark spice edge and a faint note of chocolate. Ample on the palate but soft, with ripe tannins and the fresh acid Sangiovese is built on. That acid is why it belongs with the steak for two: it cuts the fat on the rib eye and the NY strip and has enough fruit to meet the green pepper romesco without turning heavy. Good with a light chill on a warm evening under the pergola.
wines.producer: Fabrizio Pratesi farms in Carmignano, the small hill zone northwest of Florence that has been growing wine since well before it was fashionable. The family has held the Lolocco estate since 1875, and this wine takes its name from it. Ten hectares, farmed organically, on stony medium-textured ground built from alberese marly limestone, clay schist and sandstone — poor, well-drained soil that keeps the vines honest. Imported by Vinifera Imports.
wines.winemaking: Guyot-trained at 6,250 vines per hectare, organically farmed. Fermented about twenty days in temperature-controlled stainless steel, then roughly six months in steel and a rest in bottle before release. No oak, deliberately — Pratesi makes oak-aged Carmignano too, and this bottling is the one meant to show the fruit and the site straight.

wines.name: Les Marées Non-Alcoholic Sparkling Blanc de Blancs
wines.pour_notes: A real sparkling NA wine, not soda. Organic Chardonnay from Southern France. Green apple, mineral, bright. Treat it like a Blanc de Blancs — chill it, pour it tall, toast with it.
wines.producer: Les Marées is made from organic Chardonnay grown on the sunlit shores of Southern France. The maker takes the Blanc de Blancs idea (Chardonnay-only sparkling, the same backbone as Champagne) and removes the alcohol while preserving the structure.
wines.winemaking: Made in the spirit of a real sparkling wine — bright, refined, structured around green apple and mineral. Aimed at slow café afternoons, easy celebrations, and any moment that calls for sparkle without alcohol.

wines.name: Cantina Zaccagnini Alcohol-Removed White
wines.pour_notes: A premium alcohol-removed Italian white from Abruzzo. Bright straw color, yellow fruits, white flowers, delicate and balanced. Made from a real wine that's had the alcohol gently distilled out — full character, zero buzz.
wines.producer: The Ciccio Zaccagnini estate sits on 500 acres in Bolognano, about 30 miles from the Adriatic coast and 8 miles from the Maiella mountains (which rise to 9,000 ft). The vineyards are in the cru section 'Colle Morto di Bolognano.' Marcello Zaccagnini and winemaker Concezio Marulli are central figures in the modern Abruzzo wine renaissance, and every bottle of this line carries a small piece of tralcetto — grape vine — as the estate's signature.
wines.winemaking: A first-class wine is the starting point — quality in, quality out. The alcohol is removed in a two-step distillation in a vacuum evaporator: the first pass captures the volatile aromas (which evaporate first), and those aromas are condensed and held aside. The second pass evaporates the ethanol. Finally the preserved aromas are returned to the dealcoholized wine, so the finished bottle retains the original wine's character without the alcohol.

cocktails.name: Nectarine & Raspberry Gin Spritz
cocktails.tagline: gin · bianco vermouth · gran classico · soda
cocktails.pour_notes: Katie’s September drink. Terramar gin over nectarines and Swan House raspberries macerated down to their syrup, with bianco vermouth for a soft floral middle and a measure of Gran Classico for bitterness at the back. Lemon for lift, then topped with soda, so it drinks long and cold and slightly bitter while the fire comes up. Pale coral in the glass.

ingredients.name: Terramar gin
ingredients.description: Gin from Terramar Brewstillery in Edison, just down the road — an award-winning brewery and distillery set in a former slaughterhouse on the old Edison Slough oxbow. They distill it grain-to-glass from Washington-grown, craft-malted barley (the same base as their beer) and are growing their own juniper and botanicals on the property. A true neighbor pour.

ingredients.name: Nectarine and raspberry maceration
ingredients.description: Ripe nectarines and raspberries cut at Swan House, macerated with sugar until they give up their syrup. The syrup is the drink, not a sweetener added after.

ingredients.name: Bianco vermouth
ingredients.description: White vermouth, lightly sweet and floral, which rounds the fruit and softens the gin.

ingredients.name: Gran Classico
ingredients.description: A Swiss bitter in the old Turin style, built on gentian and wormwood with a bright orange edge. Where the bitterness and the colour come from; drier and more herbal than Aperol.

ingredients.name: Lemon
ingredients.description: Fresh lemon for acid and lift.

ingredients.name: Soda water
ingredients.description: Topped to length, so it stays light and cold through the welcome hour.

cocktails.name: Lavender Lemonade
cocktails.pour_notes: Lavender cut fresh at Swan House, steeped and folded into a proper lemonade — floral and cooling, tart enough to be a real drink rather than a consolation. This is the zero-proof pour for the evening, and it drinks well straight through the crudo and the caprese.

ingredients.name: Swan House lavender
ingredients.description: Lavender grown and cut at Swan House, steeped for its perfume without letting it go soapy. The most direct farm-to-glass line on the drink list.

ingredients.name: Simple syrup
ingredients.description: Sweetened just enough to balance the acid and carry the lavender.

ingredients.name: Water or soda
ingredients.description: Lengthened and served cold over ice.
